objective: Research missing slide layouts and barriers to agents dividing a slide into regions with different content types; file atomic findings.
interpretation: Spatial subdivision of one slide into content regions; pagination across multiple slides is distinct and not substituted for this request.
main_result: Raw region composition works. The default semantic/planning/discovery path does not consistently represent, recommend or supply executable mixed-region compositions, and rhythm analysis erases their structural differences. Some native-diagram placements are falsely advertised. Two researched capability opportunities are coordinated small multiples and image-source-point callouts.
causality_limit: Tool failures, accepted schemas, source constraints and control outputs were verified. These mechanisms plausibly influence authoring choices; no controlled agent experiment or representative historical traces establishes that agents never compose or measures the causal contribution of each mechanism.

findings.title: Add coordinated small-multiple line-chart composition with shared scales
findings.classification: New output capability; independent-chart behavior is not a regression
findings.scenario: A QBR compares revenue magnitudes and trends for four regions over the same quarters. One chart per region makes each trend readable without four overlapping lines; the audience must also compare absolute revenue.
findings.desired_output: 2–6 equally sized line panels with common category/time domain, shared y domain and aligned plot rectangles; one claim headline, region captions, one source line, optional explicitly disclosed independent scales.
existing_closest: Raw nested horizontal/vertical compose of diagram leaves
Raw shape_grid with multiple chart cells
findings.why_closest_insufficient: These arrange charts spatially but do not coordinate data domains, tick formats, margins, plot extents or category order. Each chart calculates its own data-dependent y scale. A card secondary chart cannot supply a common y domain either.

repro.command: cd svggen && go run ./cmd/svggen render -i ../.claude/review-evidence/2026-10-02-layout-composition/small-multiple-low.json -o ../.claude/review-evidence/2026-10-02-layout-composition/small-multiple-low.svg (repeat high)
repro.observation: Rendered and inspected both panels: identical trajectory geometry and equally tall Q4 points although the second region is ten times larger. The differing ticks truthfully disclose each independent chart but do not support the requested cross-panel magnitude comparison.
repro.explicit_domain_attempt: data.y_min=0 and data.y_max=300 both rejected UNKNOWN_FIELD by current source.
repro.tool_note: Used current source via go run. Ignored stale bin/svggen rejection of data_labels because it predates current chart schema.

root_pointers: svggen/charts.go:1866 (domain derived solely from that ChartData)
svggen/chart_schemas.go:23 (no explicit Cartesian bounds/common scale fields)
findings.ordinary_workaround: Put all regions in one multi-series line chart, or manually pre-render a coordinated external SVG and embed it. First can obscure overlapping series; second bypasses the supported renderer and automatic fit/capacity contract.
acceptance: Author 2–6 line-chart facets from shared categories and named panel values without dummy data or external plotting.
Compute the shared x/y domain once and apply it to every panel, including negative and constant data; equal values land at identical positions on equal plots.
For the supplied 10x data, common scales visibly show the magnitude difference; panel series geometry is not identical.
Use common left/right plot padding and common tick precision across panels; differing panel-title lengths do not misalign plots.
Any independent-scale option is explicit and labelled; shared scales are the comparison default.
Reject or split layouts whose panel labels or plots cannot meet current role readability floors; inspect raster outputs on at least a broad and narrow template.

findings.title: Keep exhibit callouts attached to source-image points through crop and layout changes
findings.classification: New reusable exhibit capability; arbitrary manual annotation already possible
findings.scenario: A product demo or operational case study uses one screenshot/photo as evidence. Two numbered callouts should identify a delayed queue and its status badge. The same exhibit must render on templates with different content regions and picture aspect ratios.
findings.desired_output: An evidence image with one or two readable external callout labels and leaders attached to specified source-image points, retaining correct attachment after native placement, contain/cover and template changes.
existing_closest: shape_grid image cell plus badge/arrow overlays
findings.why_closest_insufficient: Image-text-split pairs image and narrative but does not bind each statement to a location in the image. Existing overlay endpoints are slide percentages or named points on the grid-cell rectangle; no source-image coordinates or image crop transform is available to their resolver. A marker placed at one global percentage must be recomputed when frame/crop changes.
root_pointers: cmd/json2pptx/overlays.go:300 (resolveOverlayPoint uses cell rectangle or slide percentages)
internal/generator/grid_image_crop.go:13 (raster image cover crop calculated independently)
findings.ordinary_workaround: For a fixed artifact, manually compute final image position and crop, author slide-percentage arrow endpoints, and inspect every slide. Or bake callouts into an SVG/bitmap before embedding. Both create a valid static exhibit; the first becomes stale on layout/crop changes, and the second scales callout text with the picture rather than preserving the current native readability floor.
findings.specific_geometry_evidence: A 1600x900 screenshot cover-filled into a square exposes source horizontal interval [0.21875,0.78125]. A target at source x=0.25 lands at cell x≈0.05556 rather than x=0.25. The existing named cell anchors cannot express this relation and slide-percent points do not update with the frame.

Report an off-crop target instead of silently pointing at another visible region; preserve the supplied image and callout wording.
Demonstrate a product screenshot with two labelled targets in wide and square frames, with readable native labels and leaders avoiding the labels.

p-style-template-analysis.user_requirement: Always analyze p-style alongside tracked templates; local/gitignored status does not justify excluding it.

comparison.canonical_roles: p-style has all seven mandatory native roles: title→slideLayout1, content→slideLayout2, closing→slideLayout3, section→slideLayout4, two-column→slideLayout5, blank-canvas→slideLayout6, blank-title→slideLayout7. No synthesized required role.
comparison.optional_roles: p-style lacks native agenda, quote, image-left, image-right aliases. modern-yellow additionally resolves quote to its Statement layout. Existing named patterns and raw compose supply those compositions, so optional native absence is not a new missing renderer finding.
comparison.fonts: p-style title font Georgia, body Arial; normal content/blank-title titles 28pt and native content body 20pt. modern-yellow title Segoe UI Semibold/body Segoe UI; discovery body size 18pt normalized, native template body 28pt. Shape-grid role sizes still follow shared tokens.
comparison.interpretation: p-style ordinary body starts at 153.3pt, 8.2pt above modern-yellow 161.5pt; reported body width 899.3pt versus859.5pt. p-style is a meaningful wider/serif/native-font reference, not a substitute excluded in favor of a tracked template.
comparison.zone_note: Examination content_zone is a layout-derived structural rectangle. It differs from the grid content_frame body-start line and from profile reserved source/takeaway bands; preserve exact fields rather than equating all three.
comparison.closing_disclosure: p-style Closing has a separate legal_disclosure (Georgia11pt; x5197150,y4823926,w6604325,h1655540 EMU), ordinary subtitle Arial22pt, and title66pt. Disclosure must remain independently addressed and reserved.
comparison.section: p-style Section Divider has title-at-bottom/compact-title tags:48pt title max_chars_per_line14;350pt auto-filled orange Section Number. This is template variation, not missing slide composition.
